task.description:
WF-03 Step 2b -- HARD GATE on CODE-DESIGNER's fix design for ISS-0109. The design artefact is lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md. You are the only check on it before implementation begins; there is no human reviewer (core-directives.md, Humanless Operation). A validator that reads the producer's result.summary and agrees has validated nothing -- RE-DERIVE every verdict below from the code and the documents themselves.

Read: lib/letflow/design/iss0109-provisioning-completeness-and-fixture-instrumentation.md in full, then handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-02-code-designer.json, then handoffs/WF03-ISS0109-20260821/step-01-issue-fixer-diagnose.json (the diagnosis the design is built on).

Your standard checks apply (covers every acceptance criterion, contains no implementation code, unambiguous enough to build from). Beyond those, this design makes SIX specific claims that are load-bearing and individually checkable. Check each one AT THE SOURCE, and state per claim: CONFIRMED or REFUTED, with the evidence you used.

CLAIM 1 -- "Not a production defect." The design refutes the Step 1 lead that insert_or_fetch_registration/2 -> re_select_registration/1 can return {:ok, registration} for a schema that does not exist, on the grounds that provision_tenant_schema/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:164) runs CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS UNCONDITIONALLY at :188 inside the same transaction, BEFORE reaching insert_or_fetch_registration/2 at :190, so the pre-existing-row branch at :483-:488 can never return naming an absent schema. Read those lines yourself. Verify specifically: (i) that :188 is genuinely unconditional and not inside a branch skipped on the pre-existing path; (ii) that :188 and :190 are inside ONE transaction opened at :170; (iii) that no other caller reaches the registration path without going through :188. If any of the three fails, the design's central structural claim fails and this is a FAIL.

CLAIM 2 -- "Completeness is a decided invariant, not a defect." The design declines to guarantee table completeness inside provision_tenant_schema/1 because lib/letflow/design/req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md:288-294's "No implicit chaining invariant" decides it, and core-directives.md forbids silently re-deciding a decided record. Read req022's lines 288-294 yourself and confirm they actually say what the design says they say. This is the highest-risk claim in the design: if it is a misreading, the design has declined a real production fix on a false authority. If the record genuinely decides it, the design is RIGHT to decline and you must say so.

CLAIM 3 -- "C1 fails first, deterministically." The design's headline regression case drops the promotion_assertion_runs table while leaving the schema AND schema_migrations intact, and asserts that PRE-FIX the fixture still passes -- because Ecto's Migrator sees the version already recorded and re-applies nothing, so replay_migrations/1 returns {:ok, _} against an incomplete schema. This is the claim that makes the whole regression suite meaningful; if replay actually recreates the table, C1 passes pre-fix and proves nothing. Settle it: read the replay path (tenant_provisioning.ex:238-264) and Migrator's semantics, and if you can settle it by RUNNING something cheap against the test database rather than by reasoning, do that -- constructing the state and observing replay's return value is worth far more than an argument about it.

CLAIM 4 -- "The 19-table oracle is legal because of a both-directions rot guard." A hard-coded table list is exactly the kind of duplicated constant that goes stale silently. Verify: (i) the count and names actually match what the tenant migration manifest produces today -- derive the real list yourself rather than trusting the design's; (ii) the specified guard test genuinely fails in BOTH directions (a table added to the manifest but not the oracle, AND a table removed from the manifest but left in the oracle). A one-direction guard is a FAIL on this item.

CLAIM 5 -- "C2 is a characterization test, not the regression." The design flags that C2 (drop the schema, leave the registry row) proves FIXTURE detection rather than any production behaviour change. Confirm the design does not anywhere present C2 as evidence of a production fix, and that the distinction is stated where TEST-DESIGNER will actually see it.

CLAIM 6 -- SCOPE DISCIPLINE. Confirm the design proposes no fix for ISS-0110/GH#364 (reaper min_age), ISS-0111/GH#365 (identity_migration_test bulk delete), ISS-0112/GH#366 (the other 39 copy-paste sites), ISS-0113/GH#367 (Sandbox.mode(:auto) leak) or ISS-0107/GH#357 (nested mix test), AND that no part of its rationale DEPENDS on any of them being fixed. Also confirm helper adoption is limited to the two modules ISS-0109 names.

ALSO CHECK, and this one is about honesty rather than correctness: the design's FIXED-vs-INSTRUMENTED verdict says INSTRUMENTED, not FIXED, and recommends NOT closing ISS-0109. Confirm that verdict is consistent with what the design actually delivers -- i.e. that the design does not elsewhere claim or imply a root cause has been removed. ORCH sets ISS-0109's final status from this verdict, so an overstated one would put a false 'resolved' into a registry six other issues cross-reference. If you believe the verdict is WRONG IN EITHER DIRECTION -- overstated, or understated because the design does remove a real root cause -- say so.

VERDICT RULES: PASS only if every acceptance criterion is met AND all six claims are CONFIRMED. FAIL if any claim is REFUTED, naming the specific gap per acceptance criterion (not a general impression) so CODE-DESIGNER's rework is narrowly scoped. A design that is merely thinner than you would have written it is not a FAIL; a design resting on a misread source is.

CONSTRAINTS: do not edit the design yourself -- you gate it, CODE-DESIGNER reworks it. Toolchain here is Elixir 1.20.3/OTP 29 against a 1.18.3-otp-27 pin (ISS-0106, filed, not yours), so `mix format --check-formatted` and `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` fail on main for unrelated reasons; use plain `mix compile`/`mix test`. Postgres for this workspace is on LETFLOW_DB_PORT from ./.env. Branch feature/WF03-ISS0109-20260821; commit by explicit filename, never `git add -A`.
acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion of step-02-code-designer.json is checked against the design artefact itself and a per-criterion met/not-met verdict is given
The design contains no implementation code (function bodies) -- verified by reading, not assumed

CLAIM 1 (CREATE SCHEMA at tenant_provisioning.ex:188 is unconditional, inside the transaction opened at :170, and unavoidable on the pre-existing-registration path) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED against the actual source lines
CLAIM 2 (req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md:288-294 genuinely decides the no-implicit-chaining invariant) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED by reading that record directly

CLAIM 3 (C1 fails first: replay_migrations/1 returns {:ok, _} against a schema with a dropped table whose version is still recorded) is settled -- preferably by constructing the state and observing replay's actual return value rather than by argument alone
CLAIM 4 (the hard-coded table oracle matches the manifest today, and its rot guard fails in BOTH directions) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED, with the real table list derived independently
CLAIM 5 (C2 is presented as a characterization test, not as evidence of a production fix) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED
CLAIM 6 (no fix designed for ISS-0110/0111/0112/0113/0107, no rationale depending on them, helper adoption limited to the two named modules) is CONFIRMED or REFUTED
An explicit judgement is given on whether the INSTRUMENTED-not-FIXED verdict is consistent with what the design delivers, including whether it is understated
A single overall verdict (PASS or FAIL) is stated, and on FAIL each gap is named per acceptance criterion so rework is narrowly scoped

result.summary:
HARD GATE VERDICT: FAIL -- narrowly. All SIX load-bearing claims are CONFIRMED at source; the design's reasoning is sound and its INSTRUMENTED-not-FIXED verdict is honest. It fails on ONE concrete, cheap-to-fix defect in the normative interface of its own primary function.

THE DEFECT (blocks step-02 AC1 'unambiguous enough to build from' and AC3 'covers scope item (A) the shared fixture helper'). Design section 3.2 declares opts as [... status: :disabled | :active | :migrating, ...] and section 3.2 step 2 says the helper calls Tenant.create_changeset/3 with opts[:status] '(default :disabled, matching both current sites)'. Both halves are false:
  (a) lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex:56 -- field(:status, Ecto.Enum, values: [:active, :migrating], default: :active). :disabled is NOT a member of the status enum. Verified by running it: inserting a Tenant with status: :disabled returns an invalid changeset -- errors: [status: {"is invalid", [... validation: :inclusion, enum: ["active","migrating"]]}].
  (b) Neither current site passes a status at all. promotion_test.exs:62-72 and promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs:95-105 pass only %{slug:, display_name:}; the :disabled they pass is create_changeset/3's THIRD argument, the oidc_mode, not a status. The design has conflated the oidc_mode arg with the status field.
Consequence: ELIXIR-DEV following section 3.2 literally writes a helper that raises on every tenant insert, and adoption would silently change the tenant row's status away from today's default :active -- contradicting the design's own behaviour-preservation standard (section 7.7, INV-F-5/F-6). REWORK: correct the opts type and section 3.2 step 2 to match create_changeset/3's real contract (either drop :status from opts entirely, matching both sites, or restrict it to :active | :migrating with default :active, and name the oidc_mode argument separately). Nothing else in the design needs to change for this.

PER-CLAIM VERDICTS (all re-derived; the producer's result.summary was not used as evidence):
CLAIM 1 -- CONFIRMED. tenant_provisioning.ex:170 opens the single Repo.transaction/1; :174 advisory lock; :188 CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS sits at the top level of that transaction function body -- no case/if/cond wraps it, it runs on every call including the idempotent second one; :190 is the very next expression and the only call site of insert_or_fetch_registration/2 (a defp; grep over lib/ and test/ finds exactly one caller, :190), which reaches re_select_registration/1 at :471/:483. (iii) also holds at the data level: no writer to tenant_schemas exists outside this module -- every other lib/ reference (event_store/registry.ex:199, identity_migration.ex:70, sandbox_pool.ex) is a read. So the pre-existing-row branch cannot return naming an absent schema.
CLAIM 2 -- CONFIRMED, with a MINOR over-extension noted. req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md:288-294 reads verbatim: '**No implicit chaining invariant:** provision_tenant_schema/1 never calls replay_migrations/2, and replay_migrations/2 never calls provision_tenant_schema/1. They are two separate, composable steps a caller sequences explicitly...' plus the R-Co bpm_provision_tenant_schema / runForSchema justification and 'a future requirement owns the onboarding orchestration.' The record genuinely decides it; the design is RIGHT to decline the chaining fix, and right that the completeness obligation belongs to the sequencer. TWO caveats recorded as MINOR, not as the FAIL: (1) the record decides 'never CALLS', it does not literally forbid provision_tenant_schema/1 from VERIFYING tables or returning a new error; section 2.2 extends the record slightly further than its text. (2) The design cites core-directives.md's unoverridable clause, which is scoped to docs/migration/decisions/ records; req022 lives in lib/letflow/design/. Neither caveat changes the outcome -- the fixture layer really is the sequencer in both ISS-0109 failures -- so this stays CONFIRMED.
CLAIM 3 -- CONFIRMED EMPIRICALLY, not by argument. Ran a throwaway script against this workspace's Postgres (LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5472, MIX_ENV=test mix run): provisioned a tenant, replayed (31 versions, 20 relations = 19 tenant tables + schema_migrations), then DROP TABLE "<schema>"."promotion_assertion_runs" leaving the schema and every schema_migrations row intact (confirmed version 20260818090001 still present, count=1), then called TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1 again. Observed output: REPLAY#2_RESULT={:ok, []} and 'promotion_assertion_runs present after replay#2: false' (19 relations remaining). Replay returns {:ok, _} against an incomplete schema and re-creates nothing. C1 therefore does pass pre-fix and the regression suite is meaningful. Script was run from scratch/ and deleted afterwards.
CLAIM 4 -- CONFIRMED. Derived the real list independently from a freshly provisioned schema via information_schema.tables: event_idempotency, event_payload_store, event_type_registry, events, events_archive, groups, instance_definition_snapshots, instance_projections, instance_sequence, instance_state_snapshots, lua_script_execution_audit, process_definitions, promotion_assertion_runs, promotion_reviews, tasks, tenant_role, tokens, users, variable_schemas -- exactly 19, plus schema_migrations which the design correctly excludes. Set-equal to the design's section 3.3 list, no omissions or extras. The manifest count (31) matches too. (ii) The guard is specified as 'set equality in both directions' between the observed set and expected_tenant_tables/0, so a manifest addition and a manifest removal both fail it -- two-directional as required, and INV-F-7 makes removing the guard invalidate the list.
CLAIM 5 -- CONFIRMED. Section 7.2 carries an explicit 'Note on what this proves': it proves the FIXTURE detects the state, does NOT prove a production behaviour change, and the characterization assertion 'must not be labelled as' the regression assertion. That note sits inside the C2 entry of the FAIL-FIRST section -- exactly where TEST-DESIGNER reads it, not in a footnote. No other passage presents C2 as production evidence; section 2.3 and INV-F-2 state no production file is modified, and section 8.1's three 'genuinely fixed' items are all detection/attribution items.
CLAIM 6 -- CONFIRMED. Section 1.2 tables all five (ISS-0110/0111/0112/0113/0107) as out of scope with per-item reasons; section 9 items 3, 5, 7 forbid touching the reaper, test_helper.exs, the other 39 sites, and Sandbox.mode; INV-F-6 deliberately preserves today's :auto behaviour so ISS-0113 is not silently absorbed. No rationale depends on any of them being fixed -- section 8.2 states the opposite explicitly ('still open... if any of them is the real cause, this design does not stop it'). Adoption is limited to the two named modules (section 5), and the call-site counts were verified independently: promotion_test.exs 8 call sites, promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs 11 = the 19 the design claims, and drop_schema!/1 really does have a second caller at promotion_assertion_rerun_test.exs:463 (SandboxPool-held schema), so section 5's decision to keep it is correct.

INSTRUMENTED-vs-FIXED HONESTY JUDGEMENT: the verdict is HONEST IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Not overstated -- section 8.2 says the root cause remains unknown, no production defect was found, the failure was never reproduced, and the three live sharing channels are still open; section 8.3 recommends NOT closing ISS-0109; INV-F-2 and section 9 item 1 make the no-production-change claim structurally enforceable. Nothing elsewhere in the document implies a root cause was removed. Not understated either -- I checked whether the design secretly removes a real root cause and it does not: claim 1 shows the schema-existence lead is refuted by the code, and claim 3 shows the completeness gap it does close is a DETECTION gap at the fixture (replay silently returns {:ok, []} on an incomplete schema), not a production defect. ORCH can set ISS-0109's status from section 8.3 as written.

NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE: verified by reading, not assumed. The file has exactly two fenced blocks (lines 172-213 and 250-255): the first is @type/@spec declarations only, the second is a bare list of table names. No function bodies, no .ex/.exs source. MET.

STEP-02 PER-CRITERION VERDICTS: AC1 artefact exists / no implementation code -- MET on the code half, NOT MET on the buildability half (the section 3.2 status defect). AC2 file:line verdict on insert_or_fetch_registration/2 -- MET, every cited line verified. AC3 covers (A)/(B)/(C) -- NOT MET: all three are structurally present (3.2+3.5 / 3.6 / 3.3+3.4) but (A)'s normative interface is unbuildable as written. AC4 adoption limited to two modules -- MET. AC5 FAIL-FIRST PROVABILITY -- MET, and C1's premise independently verified by running it; section 7.7 honestly names the one item with no fail-first proof. AC6 FIXED vs INSTRUMENTED -- MET. AC7 no fixes for the five other issues -- MET. AC8 no contradiction with iss064 or a decisions/ record -- MET, with the MINOR precedence caveat under claim 2.

issues.description: Design section 3.2's opts type declares status: :disabled | :active | :migrating with default :disabled 'matching both current sites'. lib/letflow/identity/tenant.ex:56 allows only [:active, :migrating] (default :active), and neither current fixture passes a status -- the :disabled they pass is create_changeset/3's oidc_mode argument. Verified by running the insert: changeset invalid, validation: :inclusion. Blocks step-02 AC1/AC3; rework is confined to section 3.2.

Section 2.2 extends req022:288-294 from what it decides ('provision_tenant_schema/1 never CALLS replay_migrations/2') to a broader prohibition on provision_tenant_schema/1 verifying tables or returning a new error. The narrower record is genuine and the design's conclusion still holds via the sequencer argument, but the wording claims more authority than the record grants.

Section 2.2 invokes core-directives.md's unoverridable 'a docs/migration/decisions/ record is never overridden' clause for req022, which lives in lib/letflow/design/, not docs/migration/decisions/. The correct route for contradicting a gate-approved design artefact is REVIEWER sign-off, which the design also (correctly) says is not required here since it declines the contradiction.

Section 3.5 says capture_schema_state/1 is best-effort per field (a failing field becomes nil/[]) AND returns {:error, {:capture_failed, exception}} on any exception. The two rules do not say which wins for a single failing query. ELIXIR-DEV should be told explicitly that per-field failures degrade to nil and only a failure outside the per-field guards produces {:error, {:capture_failed, _}}.

Section 3.2 step 7 states all existing call sites destructure %{tenant_id:, schema_name:}; promotion_test.exs:464-465 destructure only %{tenant_id:}. Harmless (the return is still additive) but the statement is inaccurate.

result.next_action: Route back to CODE-DESIGNER for a narrowly-scoped rework of design section 3.2 only: correct the opts status contract to match Letflow.Identity.Tenant's real enum ([:active, :migrating], default :active) and the two current fixtures (which set no status; their :disabled is create_changeset/3's oidc_mode argument), and disambiguate capture_schema_state/1's per-field-nil vs {:error, {:capture_failed, _}} boundary. Every other section, and all six load-bearing claims, passed this gate and need no rework. Do NOT re-open sections 2, 5, 7 or 8.
